title: VeriPol flags 25 and 39 false robbery reports in Murcia and Málaga in a one-week 2017 pilot; Spain's police drop it in 2024
summary: The Spanish National Police's text-based false-report classifier flagged 25 false robberies in Murcia and 39 in Málaga in a week in June 2017 (versus 3 and 12 in the same month over the prior decad...
account: VeriPol, a model for detecting false robbery reports from their text, was developed by Complutense and Carlos III university researchers with police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados. It appeared in Knowledge-Based Systems (Quijano-Sánchez, Liberatore, Camacho-Collados and Camacho-Collados, 2018). The abstract reports a validation accuracy of 91% on more than 1,000 reports from 2015, an improvement of more than 15% over expert officers. It reports a pilot study in June 2017 showing a lower bound on empirical precision of about 83%. Scientific American (1 February 2019) reported that the one-week pilot in Murcia and Málaga detected 25 and 39 false robberies respectively. The same month over the previous decade had 3 and 12. It quoted Camacho Collados on colleagues wasting time on cases that never occurred. Civio (25 March 2025) reported that the police said that in 83.54% of reports flagged false the complainant confessed. It also reported the Interior Ministry's 2018 announcement of nationwide use. Complaints analyzed were 49,702 in 2019 with 2,338 deemed false, and 3,762 in 2022 with 511 deemed false. Use stopped on 21 October 2024 because the tool was not valid in judicial proceedings, it said. A University of Valencia report (September 2024) criticized the 1,122-report training sample, missing officer training and regional language variation. AlgorithmWatch (27 October 2020) found no independent verification of effectiveness since deployment. The pilot month carries no day.
purpose: Estimate the probability that a robbery report is false from its text to support police decisions.
developer: Universidad Complutense de Madrid and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, with Spanish National Police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados
deployer: Spanish National Police (Policía Nacional), Ministry of the Interior
segment: False robbery reports filed with police
taxonomy_note: The flagged false reports are fraud detected after filing, and independent sources document the absence of evaluation and the 2024 discontinuation.

The paper's authors include the police developer. AlgorithmWatch and Civio report that no independent verification was done before the police stopped using it in October 2024.

fields.account: VeriPol, a model for detecting false robbery reports from their text, was developed by Complutense and Carlos III university researchers with police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados. It appeared in Knowledge-Based Systems (Quijano-Sánchez, Liberatore, Camacho-Collados and Camacho-Collados, 2018). The abstract reports a validation accuracy of 91% on more than 1,000 reports from 2015, an improvement of more than 15% over expert officers. It reports a pilot study in June 2017 showing a lower bound on empirical precision of about 83%. Scientific American (1 February 2019) reported that the one-week pilot in Murcia and Málaga detected 25 and 39 false robberies respectively. The same month over the previous decade had 3 and 12. It quoted Camacho Collados on colleagues wasting time on cases that never occurred. Civio (25 March 2025) reported that the police said that in 83.54% of reports flagged false the complainant confessed. It also reported the Interior Ministry's 2018 announcement of nationwide use. Complaints analyzed were 49,702 in 2019 with 2,338 deemed false, and 3,762 in 2022 with 511 deemed false. Use stopped on 21 October 2024 because the tool was not valid in judicial proceedings, it said. A University of Valencia report (September 2024) criticized the 1,122-report training sample, missing officer training and regional language variation. AlgorithmWatch (27 October 2020) found no independent verification of effectiveness since deployment. The pilot month carries no day.

fields.account: VeriPol, a model for detecting false robbery reports from their text, was developed by Complutense and Carlos III university researchers with police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados. It appeared in Knowledge-Based Systems (Quijano-Sánchez, Liberatore, Camacho-Collados and Camacho-Collados, 2018). The abstract reports a validation accuracy of 91% on more than 1,000 reports from 2015, an improvement of more than 15% over expert officers. It reports a pilot study in June 2017 showing a lower bound on empirical precision of about 83%. Scientific American (1 February 2019) reported that the one-week pilot in Murcia and Málaga detected 25 and 39 false robberies respectively. The same month over the previous decade had 3 and 12. It quoted Camacho Collados on colleagues wasting time on cases that never occurred. Civio (25 March 2025) reported that the police said that in 83.54% of reports flagged false the complainant confessed. It also reported the Interior Ministry's 2018 announcement of nationwide use. Complaints analyzed were 49,702 in 2019 with 2,338 deemed false, and 3,762 in 2022 with 511 deemed false. Use stopped on 21 October 2024 because the tool was not valid in judicial proceedings, it said. A University of Valencia report (September 2024) criticized the 1,122-report training sample, missing officer training and regional language variation. AlgorithmWatch (27 October 2020) found no independent verification of effectiveness since deployment. The pilot month carries no day.

produced_by: Training on 1,122 robbery reports from 2015 (534 genuine, 588 false) labeled by one experienced officer
